Topici, 5 συστοιχα dicuntur, quæ proprie cognata dixeris, ut justitia,justus: ubi adverbia é nominibus nata,vocat πτῶσις,casus:sed postea in aliis Topicis & in Rhetoricis,differentiam illam contempsit. Cicero in Topicis,quę videri vult ab Aristotele 10 transtulisse, συζυγια και συζυγίαν,conjugata & cõjugatione dicit: Verbum tamen Ciceronis, quanvis Aristotelis verbo non tam responderet: atta men magis est in hac re tritum & usitatû. Locus conjugatorum parciús appellatur in bibliothe- 15 ca Aristotelis, particula ejus quædam, paronyma sunt in Categoriis, ut á Grammatica grammaticus, á fortitudine fortis: in Topicis nominatim citatur decies & quinquies. hæc tautologia est quidẽ tam multiplex,quám dixi:sed tautologia feré tantûm nominis,nullius auté proli xioris doćtrinæ: sed tamẽ hæc tautologia ex lege λαβὸντ πρῶτον amputatur á P. page.notes: Line numbers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 are marginal line markers, transcribed as notes at their positions. Greek words are transcribed as best legible; the 30 marker follows "con-". Some Greek words in the text (συστοιχα, πτῶσις, συζυγία, λαβὸν πρῶτον) are doubtful and may be inexact.
